Alert.Title: Possible Port Scan Detected
Alert.Explanation: Source host 192.168.1.200 sent traffic to 21 distinct destination ports on target 10.0.0.1 within 10.0s. This pattern strongly resembles an automated port probe or service discovery sweep.
Alert.Recommendation: Inspect the source IP address in firewall logs. Determine if the host is an authorized vulnerability scanner or network inventory tool. Verify that perimeter access controls restrict unneeded exposed ports.
Alert.Disclaimer: This alert indicates suspicious traffic behavior detected by transparent deterministic heuristics, not confirmed host compromise or malicious intrusion.

Alert.Title: Connection Initiation Burst
Alert.Explanation: Source host 192.168.1.100 generated 151 connection attempts within a short interval, exceeding the baseline threshold of 50 connections.
Alert.Recommendation: Review application behavior on the originating host. Determine if this burst correlates with a legitimate scheduled job, API batch load, or an aggressive client retry loop.
Alert.Disclaimer: This alert indicates suspicious traffic behavior detected by transparent deterministic heuristics, not confirmed host compromise or malicious intrusion.

Alert.Title: Repeated TCP SYN Activity (Potential SYN Flood)
Alert.Explanation: Observed 47 TCP SYN packets with only 1 completed/terminated session packets (ratio 47.0:1). This indicates half-open connection attempts or SYN flooding.
Alert.Recommendation: Enable TCP SYN cookies on receiving endpoints and verify perimeter anti-DDoS rate limiting to prevent TCP connection pool starvation.
Alert.Disclaimer: This alert indicates suspicious traffic behavior detected by transparent deterministic heuristics, not confirmed host compromise or malicious intrusion.

Alert.Title: Suspicious / Uncommon Port Activity
Alert.Explanation: Traffic detected on monitored or sensitive administrative/legacy ports: [21, 23, 4444]. These ports are frequently targeted for exploit payloads, remote administration, or IRC control channels.
Alert.Recommendation: Audit traffic to verify if legacy services (Telnet/FTP) or unexpected listeners are intentionally running. Block unapproved ingress ports at the perimeter firewall.

Alert.Title: High Volume ICMP Traffic (Flood Indicator)
Alert.Explanation: Recorded 35 ICMP packets, surpassing the threshold of 30 packets. Rapid ICMP rates are characteristic of ping sweeps or ICMP flood degradation.
Alert.Recommendation: Apply ICMP rate-limiting on network interfaces and edge routers. Ensure ping requests do not degrade bandwidth.
Alert.Disclaimer: This alert indicates suspicious traffic behavior detected by transparent deterministic heuristics, not confirmed host compromise or malicious intrusion.

Alert.Title: Abnormally Large DNS Query (Tunneling Indicator)
Alert.Explanation: Observed 1 DNS queries containing query names >= 60 characters. Abnormally long query labels are commonly utilized in DNS covert tunneling or base-encoded data exfiltration.
Alert.Recommendation: Inspect recursive resolver query logs for high-entropy subdomains. Configure DNS response rate limiting (RRL) and DNS inspection policies to block unauthorized tunneling protocols.
Alert.Disclaimer: This alert indicates suspicious traffic behavior detected by transparent deterministic heuristics, not confirmed host compromise or malicious intrusion.

Alert.Title: Unencrypted Cleartext Protocol In Use
Alert.Explanation: Detected unencrypted application protocols (FTP, HTTP, Telnet) in network traffic. Transmitting traffic without TLS encryption exposes headers and URLs to eavesdropping and interception.
Alert.Recommendation: Migrate plain HTTP, FTP, and Telnet communications to modern encrypted standards: HTTPS (TLS 1.3), SFTP/SCP, and SSH.
Alert.Disclaimer: This alert indicates suspicious traffic behavior detected by transparent deterministic heuristics, not confirmed host compromise or malicious intrusion.

Alert.Title: High Single-Source Traffic Concentration

Alert.Recommendation: Verify whether the concentrated traffic pattern reflects ordinary endpoint behavior (e.g. streaming, backup agent, speedtest) or an unthrottled sender.
